panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 8 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H). A: Chest radiograph from the confirmed tracheobronchial amyloidosis patient showing left lung collapse with mediastinal shift, consistent with post-obstructive lobar atelectasis secondary to airway amyloidosis. B: HRCT from the same patient confirming left lung collapse and compensatory right lung hyperinflation, a direct consequence of central airway obstruction from tracheobronchial amyloidosis. C: Coronal CT mediastinal window from the confirmed amyloidosis patient demonstrating speckled calcification in the tracheobronchial wall, a recognized CT feature of tracheobronchial amyloidosis. D: Axial CT mediastinal window from the same patient confirming speckled tracheobronchial wall calcification, characteristic of amyloid deposition in the airway wall. E: Bronchoscopic view from the confirmed patient showing deformed tracheal anatomy, narrowed main bronchi, and typical yellow friable lesions bleeding on touch — the classic...
